content.user_title: Coordinate Parallel Agents With Fewer Conflicts
content.value_statement: Parallel coding agents often collide in shared files and documentation. This skill provides structural and editing practices that reduce merge conflicts.
actual_capabilities: Structures new behavior into separate files with minimal shared registration edits.
Guides stable edits to registries, dispatchers, generated files, and lockfiles.
Identifies high-churn hub files using Git history and file size.
Plans behavior-preserving splits of shared code into concern-focused files.
Prunes and shards AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, README, and module documentation.
Explains how to resolve shared-file conflicts without dropping either branch's intent.
limitations: Provides workflow guidance but does not coordinate agents or merge branches automatically.
Requires repository context and Git history for meaningful hotspot analysis.
Does not replace project-specific formatting, testing, or code review requirements.
Cannot guarantee conflict-free merges when agents change the same behavior.

use_cases.title: Add Concurrent Features
use_cases.description: Plan feature files and minimal registration edits before multiple agents begin implementation.

use_cases.title: Refactor Conflict Hotspots
use_cases.description: Measure repository churn and split hub files without changing behavior.
use_cases.target_user: Maintainer of a busy shared repository

use_cases.title: Reduce Documentation Churn
use_cases.description: Keep durable invariants in root instructions and move module details closer to their code.
use_cases.target_user: Documentation owner for an agent-managed codebase

prompt_templates.title: Place a New Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature request and repository layout. Recommend a new file location and the smallest required shared-file registration edit.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Parallel Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Split these tasks among parallel agents. Identify shared files, assign ownership, and describe edits that should merge independently.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Conflict Hotspots
prompt_templates.prompt: Use recent Git history and file sizes to rank likely conflict hubs. Classify each as a hub, hot concern, or generated file.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Safe Hub Split
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this shared hub and propose a behavior-preserving split. Include file boundaries, move order, validation steps, documentation updates, and branch coordination.

output_examples.input: Two agents need to add independent HTTP resources to one router.
output_examples.output: Create one handler file per resource. Give each agent one router registration line, preserve stable ordering, then run formatting and route tests.

output_examples.input: A large command dispatcher appears in most recent feature commits.
output: Classification: likely hub because unrelated features repeatedly modify the same dispatcher.
Split: move each command handler into its own file and retain only delegating entries.
Validation: format the moved files, run the full test suite, and confirm every command remains registered.

output_examples.input: The root agent instructions contain module inventories and progress notes.
output_examples.output: Remove discoverable inventories and temporary status. Keep durable invariants at the root, then move module-specific guidance into nearby documentation.

best_practices: Give each new behavior its own file and keep shared registration edits minimal.
Separate behavior-preserving moves from feature changes and land them when parallel work is quiet.
Run canonical formatters and tests after resolving conflicts or regenerating generated files.
anti_patterns: Do not append unrelated implementation bodies to a shared dispatcher, router, or test main.
Do not hand-merge generated files or lockfiles; regenerate them with the owning tool.
Do not mix repository-wide formatting or documentation cleanup into a feature change.

faq.question: Does this skill run multiple agents?
faq.answer: No. It provides repository structure and collaboration guidance for agents that already work in parallel.

faq.question: Which shared files does it address?
faq.answer: It covers dispatchers, routers, registries, shared tests, generated files, lockfiles, and root documentation.

faq.question: How does it identify a hub file?
faq.answer: It combines recent Git churn with file size, then checks whether unrelated features repeatedly touch the same file.

faq.question: Should every hot file be split?
faq.answer: No. Active concerns and generated files can have legitimate churn, so classification should happen before refactoring.

faq.question: How should generated-file conflicts be handled?
faq.answer: Choose one side as a base, regenerate with the owning tool, and validate the resulting output.

faq.question: What belongs in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md?
faq.answer: Keep durable invariants and non-obvious lessons. Move module details nearby and omit temporary state or easily discovered inventories.
